title: CakewordAI
summary: Point at anything to learn its name in any language
content: CakewordAI: Point at anything to learn its name in any language | Product Hunt Launching today CakewordAI Launching today Point at anything to learn its name in any language 240 followers Point at anything to learn its name in any language 240 followers Visit website Language Learning Kids point the camera at anything — a cup, a teddy bear, a guitar — and Cakeword cuts it out into a sticker, says its name in the language they're learning, and adds it to their Word Dex. 100% on-device AI. No accounts, no ads, no data collection. Overview Reviews Alternatives Team Awards More Free Launch tags: Kids • Artificial Intelligence • Tech Launch Team Show more Show more Launching Today # 4 Day Rank Upvote • 173 points Follow CakewordAI Add to collection Share Analytics Company Info apps.apple.com/de/app/cakeword-snap-learn/id6775628982 App Store CakewordAI Info Launched in 2026 Forum p/cakewordai-snap-learn Similar Products Felo Translator A real time translation APP by AI(GPT - 4) 4.8 ( 6 reviews ) Translate Now Effortlessly translate any language. 5.0 ( 3 reviews ) WordSnap - AI Flashcards Maker Visual Vocabulary Builder 5.0 ( 1 review ) Note and writing apps Writing assistants My First 150 Words A fun way to teach young children their first 150 words! 5.0 ( 1 review ) Travel Buddy Help kids learn new words using camera with a SayIt button View more Subscribe Sign in Krisp Voice Translation Speech-to-speech translation API Try Krisp Voice Translation Promoted What do you think? … Login to comment Worathiti Pung LaterAI Maker 📌 Hi Product Hunt! 👋 Cakeword started with a simple observation: kids don't learn words from flashcards, they learn from things. The cup they drink from, the teddy they sleep with, the guitar in the corner. So I built an app that turns the real world into the deck. How it works: your kid points the camera at any object and snaps it. Cakeword cuts the object out of the photo into a die-cut sticker, names it in the language they're learning and their native language, and says it out loud. The sticker lands in their collection, tilted and hand-placed, like a real sticker book. Then Pokémon happens. There's a Word Dex of 102 everyday objects across themed sets, Food, Animals, Toys, Vehicles — and kids hunt them down around the house. There are streaks, badges, collector levels, a catch-of-the-day… and rare ✨shiny✨ catches that show up about one snap in twelve and lose their minds (in a good way). My favorite emergent behavior from testing: kids start searching the house for things they haven't caught yet. The app turns "go play" into "go find me a spoon, in German." The part I'm proudest of: everything runs on-device. Object recognition and cut-out happen with Apple's Vision framework, naming and translation with the on-device Apple Intelligence model, speech with the system synthesizer. There is no server. Which means: - 🔒 Photos of your home and your kid's stuff never leave the phone - 🙅 No account, no ads, no analytics, no tracking —

content: pleNx — Plex client for Nintendo Switch: The first native Plex client for Nintendo Switch | Product Hunt Launched this week pleNx — Plex client for Nintendo Switch Launched this week The first native Plex client for Nintendo Switch 121 followers The first native Plex client for Nintendo Switch 121 followers Visit website pleNx is a free, open-source, native Plex client for the Nintendo Switch. Browse your server, queue your watchlist, download for offline in original quality, and play with MPV — handheld or docked on any TV. Overview Reviews Alternatives Team More Free Launch tags: Nintendo • Open Source • Streaming Services Launch Team Show more Show more Launched this week # 17 Day Rank Upvote • 86 points Follow pleNx — Plex client for Nintendo Switch Add to collection Share Company Info thcolin.github.io/pleNx GitHub pleNx — Plex client for Nintendo Switch Info Launched in 2026 Forum p/plenx-plex-client-for-nintendo-switch Similar Products Plex Enjoy your media on all your devices. 4.4 ( 5 reviews ) Video hosting platforms File storage and sharing apps Netflix Watch TV shows and movies online. 4.3 ( 11 reviews ) Video hosting platforms VLC Media Player Free Multimedia Solutions for all OS 4.8 ( 5 reviews ) Nintendo A company of video games and consoles. 4.8 ( 4 reviews ) Physical Products Games Infuse An elegant video player 4.0 ( 1 review ) Video editing Video hosting platforms View more Subscribe Sign in Customer.io Automate Messaging Everywhere — Startups Get 12 Months Free Try Customer.io Promoted What do you think? … Login to comment Thomas Colin pleNx — Plex client for Nintendo Switch Maker 📌 Hi! 👋 This project started when I discovered tico, which brought native GameCube emulation to the Nintendo Switch. That made the Switch everything I'd wanted: one device for modern games and retro gaming all the way up to the GameCube. The only thing missing was my media — browsing, streaming and downloading from my Plex server. I was already doing it through an Android dual boot, but rebooting into another OS just to watch something never felt right. The goal: when I leave on vacation and want to pack light, I just grab the Switch and I have everything — and once docked, it doubles as an offline media player for any TV. No native Plex client existed for the Switch, so I built one. pleNx is a fork of Switchfin (an open-source Jellyfin client) migrated entirely to the Plex API and redesigned — entirely built with Claude Code (Fable 5) in 48 hours, with me reviewing, testing on real hardware and steering the design. What it does: * 🎬 Your server's home hubs, libraries, collections and search, fully controller-driven * ⭐ Plex Watchlist — browse, sort, add/remove * ⬇️ Offline downloads in original quality (a full season in one tap) * ▶️ MPV playback — direct play or transcode through your own server, subtitles, audio tracks * 🖥️ Same codebase runs on Windows, macOS, Linux and Android Fair warning: on the Switch it's homebrew, so the console needs custom

content: ShellMate: Manage SSH servers, credentials, and teams in one place | Product Hunt Launched this week ShellMate Launched this week Manage SSH servers, credentials, and teams in one place 201 followers Manage SSH servers, credentials, and teams in one place 201 followers Visit website Terminals ShellMate is a modern SSH workspace with native terminal sessions, permission-aware team access, server-managed encrypted credentials, and auditable connection controls. Overview Reviews Alternatives Built with Team More Free Options Launch tags: Productivity • Privacy • Developer Tools Launch Team / Built With Show more Show more Launched this week # 8 Day Rank Upvote • 118 points Follow ShellMate Add to collection Share Company Info shellmate.net ShellMate Info Launched in 2026 Forum p/shellmate-2 Similar Products 1Password The world’s most-loved password manager 4.8 ( 45 reviews ) Password managers Security software Bitwarden Open Source Password Management for You and Your Business. 4.8 ( 16 reviews ) Password managers Infisical Helping dev teams sync environment variables 5.0 ( 3 reviews ) Security software Databases and backend frameworks APX Terminal Encrypted terminal and SSH client with built‑in AI assistant Terminals Server Explorer An explorer for your Unix Server, with Editors and CLI View more Subscribe Sign in Framer Launch websites with enterprise needs at startup speeds. Try Framer Promoted What do you think? … Login to comment Arab ShellMate Maker 📌 Hey Product Hunt! 👋 ShellMate started from a frustration I ran into almost every day. Connecting to servers via SSH was easy — everything around it wasn't. Credentials were in password managers, notes were scattered across documents, access details lived in chat messages, and onboarding teammates was often a manual process. Finding the right server sometimes took longer than connecting to it. So I built ShellMate, a desktop SSH workspace for developers, sysadmins, and DevOps teams. It brings hosts, credentials, terminal sessions, permissions, team collaboration, and access management into one place. A quick note on security: I previously described the credential vault as "zero-knowledge." That wasn't accurate. ShellMate currently uses server-managed encryption and short-lived, session-bound access grants. The server remains part of the trust boundary, so it is not yet a true zero-knowledge or end-to-end encrypted system. What ShellMate offers today: 🔐 Encrypted credential storage with session-bound access ⚡ Fast desktop SSH experience 🛡️ Permission-aware host access and short-lived grants 👥 Team workspaces, host groups, and RBAC 🖥️ Organized host and infrastructure management 📋 Activity logs and security events 🔑 SSH certificate support for enrolled hosts I'm actively working toward a stronger end-to-end encrypted architecture while keeping the experience simple and fast. I'd love your feedback: 👉 What's the biggest pain point in your current SSH workflow? 👉 What security controls would you expec
